title: SuffixDecoding: Extreme Speculative Decoding for Emerging AI Applications (Sec. 4.4 ablations, App. B)
quote: the acceptance rate does not change much even when the suffix tree size varies across almost two orders of magnitude
proves: Authors already ablate (a) global-only vs per-request-only vs both on AgenticSQL ('the global tree outperforms the per-request tree on all tasks except for Combine') and (b) tree size 256 to 10,000 output examples: speedup rises with size while acceptance rate is nearly flat. App. B proposes LRU eviction ('incorporate cache eviction (e.g. LRU)') but evaluates no eviction policy; claims ~31 days of tokens fit per A100 host (144 GB CPU RAM).
does_not_prove: No eviction-policy comparison, no Belady/oracle gap, no persistence/warm-start study; size sweep is on offline output examples, not on live multi-agent interleaved traces; global-vs-local split is per task in a figure, not per accepted token on SWE traces.
bearing: C5: Narrows. Kills the 'does global matter' half on AgenticSQL (global wins) and shows acceptance flat vs size, which shrinks the room for a better eviction policy; policy/oracle gap and persistence stay open.

title: OmniDraft: A Cross-vocabulary, Online Adaptive Drafter for On-device Speculative Decoding (App. D.5, Table 14)
quote: LFU plateaus at an earlier stage, with performance matching the full cache even with a quarter of the size.
proves: Published eviction-policy ablation for an online n-gram draft cache: on MBPP+HumanEval, acceptance 0.219 no cache, 0.254 LRU vs 0.259 LFU at 1/4 size, 0.261 vs 0.263 at 1/2, 0.267 full; speedup 1.29x to 1.33-1.36x. Policy gap is about 0.005 acceptance.
does_not_prove: On-device single-user n-gram cache, not a cross-request global suffix tree on agentic traces; no oracle policy; small benchmarks.
bearing: C5: Threatens novelty of 'compare eviction policies for a draft cache' and suggests the policy gap is tiny; does not cover suffix trees or multi-tenant agent traffic.

title: ArcticInference suffix_decoding/cache.py (SuffixDecodingCache)
quote: Evict the first eligible request. Should be FIFO order in Python 3.7+ since dict preserves insertion order.
proves: Eviction is whole-request FIFO keyed on max_cached_requests (negative = unbounded, 0 = no global cache); speculate() queries the per-request tree and the global tree separately and keeps the draft with the higher score, so the source of each draft is recoverable with a one-line change.
does_not_prove: No reuse-aware policy, no byte-based cap, no persistence/serialization API seen; does not say how often global drafts win in practice.
bearing: C5: Confirms FIFO-only baseline and that per-source attribution is cheap to instrument; supports the simulation plan.

title: ArcticInference suffix_decoding/simulator.py
venue: GitHub snowflakedb/ArcticInference (main; last change 2025-10-13 per commit history)
quote: help="Evict a fraction of the cached sequences before running requests"
proves: An offline acceptance simulator already ships with knobs --max-cached-requests, --evict-fraction, --evict-strategy {random, oldest, newest}, --use-cached-prompt; it replays ground-truth responses with greedy tree verification and logs match_len, accepted tokens, spec/update ms per step.
does_not_prove: Eviction is a one-shot fraction removed after warm-up, not online policy under a cap; no LRU/LFU/oracle; eval requests run sequentially (no interleaving); does not log global-vs-local source. No published results from it found.
bearing: C5: Narrows. The cheapest decisive test is mostly a few edits to an existing tool, so the contribution must be the findings (oracle gap, interleaved agent traces), not the harness.

title: vLLM docs: Speculative Decoding (suffix decoding options)
quote: Maximum number of requests cached in the global suffix tree. Set `0` to disable the global cache.
proves: vLLM exposes suffix_decoding_max_cached_requests (default 10000, 10x lower than Arctic's 100000) and suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth (default 24).
does_not_prove: Page says nothing about eviction policy or persistence across restarts.
bearing: C5: Confirms capacity is a user knob with no guidance; supports the capacity-curve question.

title: Suffix decoding drafts almost nothing under PP: the per-step decode rotation destroys each request's suffix tree (vllm-rbln issue 1084)
quote: a rejoining request evicts its own cached response first
proves: In vLLM's suffix proposer, a request absent from the input batch is treated as finished and its per-request tree is destroyed; under PP=4 rotation acceptance fell from 97.4% (concurrency 1) to 4.5% (concurrency 4); max_cached_requests=10000 vs 0 made no difference (51 vs 52 accepted). A patch restored 79.1% acceptance and 58.73 to 99.68 tok/s. Closed not planned (stale) 2026-10-18.
does_not_prove: Vendor fork under PP; upstream vLLM behaviour under ordinary preemption not tested here; single reporter.
bearing: C5 (and C7): Supports that per-request tree loss on preemption/rotation is real and large, which is a stronger and narrower gap than global eviction policy.

title: Beat the long tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training
quote: moderate windows (16 or 32) strike a better balance between acceptance and latency
proves: Suffix-tree drafter for RL rollouts uses a sliding window of recent trajectories with per-problem trees and down-weighting of older matches; window ablation (16, 32, all): larger windows raise acceptance but window_all has the highest latency.
does_not_prove: Window is in RL iterations, tied to policy drift; no memory cap, no eviction-policy comparison, no serving/multi-tenant setting.
bearing: C5: Prior art for recency-based retention of a suffix draft cache; narrows novelty of 'recency vs capacity' claims.

title: SAM Decoding: Speculative Decoding via Suffix Automaton
quote: we constructed a static suffix automaton based on the Vicuna-7B generation results
proves: Static (offline corpus) plus dynamic (per-generation) suffix automata; ablation on Spec-Bench: removing the static module drops speedup 1.84x to 1.64x, removing the dynamic module drops it to 1.33x; static automaton supplies drafts in 2.45% of cases.
does_not_prove: No corpus size, memory, or eviction/update policy for the static store; Spec-Bench, not agentic traffic.
bearing: C5: Supports the hypothesis that the per-request (dynamic) store does most of the work on general traffic; does not settle agentic traffic.

title: nebius/SWE-agent-trajectories
quote: The dataset is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license.
proves: 80,036 SWE-agent trajectories, 1.11 GB, CC BY 4.0; fields include instance_id, model_name (e.g. swe-agent-llama-70b), trajectory (full reasoning/action/observation log), generated_patch.
does_not_prove: Trajectory is a single string log, not token-level outputs from one tokenizer; no timestamps, so arrival interleaving must be synthesized; outputs are from older open models.
bearing: C5: Makes trace-replay simulation feasible on CPU with a permissive license.

title: nvidia/SWE-Hero-openhands-trajectories
quote: This dataset is governed by the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0).
proves: 34,269 OpenHands trajectories over 11,766 issues, ~2.4 GB parquet, generated by Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct; trajectory is a role-tagged message list (assistant actions, tool observations), so assistant outputs can be tokenized and replayed per turn.
does_not_prove: No timing; one generator model, so cross-model/tenant diversity is absent; many trajectories per issue may inflate global-cache hits versus real traffic.
bearing: C5: Best-fit public multi-turn agent trace for global-vs-local suffix attribution; caveat on duplicated issues.

title: nvidia/Nemotron-SWE-v1
quote: The trajectories were synthesized using state-of-the-art Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct.
proves: ~59k agent trajectories (card), ~11 GB, CC BY 4.0 with some BSD-3-Clause subsets; messages list plus execute_bash tool schema.
does_not_prove: Row counts on the card conflict (24,875 vs 34,772 vs 59k); fetch could not confirm tool outputs are included.
bearing: C5: Second permissive agent trace source; same single-generator caveat.

title: A First Look at Bugs in LLM Inference Engines
quote: Testing LLM inference engines requires diverse oracles beyond mere crash detection.
proves: 929 bugs from 5 engines (incl. vLLM, TensorRT-LLM); 28 root causes; no speculative-decoding, preemption, or scheduling category; closest: Concurrency Issue 39 (~4.2%), Incorrect Cache Management 11 (~1.2%), Inconsistent Output 17 (~1.8%); notes outputs vary 'even after disabling all randomness settings'.
does_not_prove: Only first 100k of 142k characters read; mined bugs predate the 2026 spec+async+hybrid cluster; no test harness built.
bearing: C7: Supports novelty: the main empirical bug study has no spec-decode or preemption class and calls for better oracles.

title: Continuous Discovery of Vulnerabilities in LLM Serving Systems with Fuzzing (GRIEF)
quote: lets new variants (e.g. EAGLE-3, Medusa) and entirely new serving modes reuse
proves: Greybox fuzzer for vLLM and SGLang using timed multi-request traces, KV-utilization/scheduler-pressure feedback, and replay-based logprob confirmation of output divergence; 15 potential vulnerabilities, 10 confirmed, 2 CVEs; 7 state-corruption bugs (cross-request KV reuse). Preemption occurs only incidentally; speculative decoding is named as future adapter work and no spec bugs are reported.
does_not_prove: Does not inject preemption/offload at chosen step boundaries, does not check acceptance equivalence, does not cover spec decode.
bearing: C7: Biggest novelty threat. Narrows C7 to 'spec-aware state-event injection with acceptance oracle'; a GRIEF spec adapter could pre-empt it quickly.

title: vLLM docs: Batch Invariance
quote: Batch invariance is currently in beta.
proves: Batch-invariant mode exists in vLLM (beta; NVIDIA CC>=8.0, AMD Instinct, Intel XPU with Triton), with TP limits and a performance cost.
does_not_prove: Page does not mention speculative decoding, preemption, or prefix caching, so whether greedy spec+preemption runs are bitwise comparable under it is undocumented. Not available on Metal.
bearing: C7: Neutral; the oracle precondition (bitwise-equal greedy runs) is not documented for spec decode.

title: SGLang docs: Deterministic Inference
quote: Radix Cache Consistency mode: test radix cache determinism (cached vs uncached prefill)
proves: SGLang deterministic mode supports CUDA graph, chunked prefill, radix cache (FA3, Triton; not FlashInfer) and temp>0; its built-in tests check same prompt across batch sizes, prefix lengths, and cached vs uncached prefill.
does_not_prove: No mention of speculative decoding, EAGLE, preemption, or retraction; its tests do not move state mid-request.
bearing: C7: Supports gap: SGLang's determinism checks stop at prefill caching; no retract/resume or spec coverage.

title: Towards Deterministic Inference in SGLang and Reproducible RL Training (LMSYS blog)
proves: Future-work list covers faster kernels, MoE, on-policy RL, radix cache, TP, FlexAttention; speculative decoding and preemption/retraction are not mentioned at all.
does_not_prove: Absence claim only; quote not captured verbatim by fetch tool.
bearing: C7: Weak support that deterministic-mode roadmaps do not target spec or retraction.

title: Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference (Thinking Machines Lab)
quote: all of our 1000 completions are identical
proves: Batch-invariant kernels made 1000 temp-0 Qwen3-235B completions identical (80 unique without); attention must be invariant to chunked prefill and prefix caching splits.
does_not_prove: No mention of speculative decoding or preemption; does not address verify-shape changes (1+k tokens) or draft-model state.
bearing: C7: Supplies the oracle precondition in principle; leaves spec/preemption untreated.

title: vLLM tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py
quote: Test consistency and acceptance rates with some different combos of preemption, executor, async scheduling, prefill chunking, spec decoding model length.
proves: vLLM CI already runs a differential test: EAGLE-3 (k=2) and ngram_gpu (k=3) runs with forced preemption (num_gpu_blocks_override=33, ~34 concurrent prompts), async scheduling, uni/mp executor and chunking are compared to a non-spec baseline on token outputs, logprobs, and acceptance rate (within 5%, 10% on ROCm), under FP32 matmul and FlexAttention.
does_not_prove: Preemption is induced by pressure, not injected at chosen step boundaries; covers only EAGLE-3 and ngram_gpu (no suffix, MTP, DFlash, draft_model, hybrid GDN/Mamba, KV offload, PD handoff); acceptance tolerance of 5% would hide small silent acceptance loss.
bearing: C7: Narrows hard. The 'compare against uninterrupted run, outputs + acceptance' oracle exists in vLLM CI; the remaining gap is step-targeted injection and coverage of hybrid/offload/PD/suffix paths.

title: [Test] Rework e2e async scheduling tests (vLLM PR 28744)
quote: Various improvements, more selective combos of features.
proves: The preemption x spec x async consistency suite dates from Nov 2025 (merged 2025-11-15).
does_not_prove: PR text does not list the combos; content inferred from the test file (I18).
bearing: C7: Shows the differential suite is ~1 year old, not new.

title: [BugFix] Fix num_output_placeholders preemption underflow (vLLM PR 48245)
quote: Reproduces deterministically with PP + async scheduling under KV pressure
proves: Stale in-flight spec output returning after KV-pressure preemption underflowed counters and crashed EngineCore, most visible with spec decode/PP at high concurrency; found on GLM-5.2-FP8 TP4/PP2 with MTP at concurrency 32-128, not by the CI suite; regression tests added (test_kv_pressure_preemption_with_inflight_output, num_spec in {0,3}).
does_not_prove: A crash, not silent divergence; regression tests are scheduler-level unit tests for this one path.
bearing: C7: Supports that the existing differential suite missed a spec+preemption bug found only at scale; also shows fixes add point regressions rather than a systematic harness.

title: LLM-42: Enabling Determinism in LLM Inference with Verified Speculation
quote: When the verifier detects a mismatch, LLM-42 rolls the sequence back to the last matching token.
proves: Determinism via decode-verify-rollback with the same model; recomputation overhead 6.81% at window 32, 46.41% at 256.
does_not_prove: Does not address preemption or separate-drafter speculative decoding; it is a determinism mechanism, not a test method.
bearing: C7: Tangential; shows rollback-based determinism is studied, but not equivalence of spec state across preemption.
